questions.def: 'Such' modifies a noun phrase; 'so' modifies an adjective/adverb.
questions.question: It was ___ a difficult test that many failed.

questions.def: 'So' is used before an adjective to express a degree.
questions.question: The music was ___ loud that I couldn't hear myself think.

questions.def: 'Enough' follows the adjective it modifies, not precedes it.
questions.question: He is enough tall to reach the top shelf.

questions.def: 'Adjective + enough' is the correct word order.
questions.question: The lecture wasn't ___ to keep me awake.

questions.def: 'Too' means more than is necessary or desirable.
questions.question: There are ___ many people here; it's crowded.

questions.def: 'So...as to' expresses purpose or result in formal contexts.
questions.question: She is ___ kind ___ help everyone.

questions.def: 'So' modifies an adjective directly.
questions.question: The party was ___ that the neighbors complained.

questions.def: 'So much' is used with uncountable nouns like money.
questions.question: He has ___ money that he doesn't know what to do with it.

questions.def: 'Such' is used before 'a/an + adjective + noun'.
questions.question: It was ___ a beautiful day that we went to the beach.

questions.def: 'Adjective + enough' is the correct word order.
questions.question: He isn't ___ for the job.

questions.def: 'Too' is used with 'to' to indicate excessiveness.
questions.question: This problem is ___ complicated for me to understand.

questions.def: 'Enough' indicates that something is sufficient.
questions.question: There weren't ___ chairs for everyone to sit down.

questions.def: Use 'such' before 'a/an + adjective + noun'.
questions.question: It's so a beautiful painting that I want to buy it.

questions.def: 'Adjective + enough' is the correct word order.
questions.question: You need to be ___ to deal with children.

questions.def: 'So' modifies an adverb to express a degree.
questions.question: She spoke ___ quickly that I couldn't understand her.

questions.def: 'So little' expresses a small quantity.
questions.question: He had ___ little time to finish the project.

questions.def: 'Enough' usually follows adjectives but precedes nouns.
questions.question: I don't have ___ to buy a new car.

questions.def: 'Such' is used before 'a/an + adjective + noun'.
questions.question: It was ___ a surprise party that she cried.

questions.def: 'Too' implies something is excessive or undesirable.
questions.question: This book is ___ boring for me to finish it.

questions.def: Use 'such' before 'a/an + adjective + noun'.
questions.question: She is so intelligent woman that everyone admires her.

questions.def: 'Enough' usually follows adjectives but precedes nouns.
questions.question: We didn't get ___ to make a decision.

questions.def: 'So' modifies an adjective to express a degree.
questions.question: The task wasn't ___ difficult for him to complete.

questions.def: 'Too' means more than is necessary or desirable.
questions.question: There were ___ many applicants for the job.

questions.def: 'Adjective + enough' is the correct word order.
questions.question: She isn't ___ to perform the surgery.

questions.def: 'So many' is used with countable nouns like books.
questions.question: He has ___ many books to read.

questions.def: 'So' modifies an adjective to express a degree.
questions.question: The movie was ___ long that I fell asleep.

questions.def: "So" modifies adjectives; "such" modifies noun phrases.
questions.question: The coffee was ___ hot that I burnt my tongue.

questions.def: "Such" precedes "a/an + adjective + noun".
questions.question: It was ___ a beautiful day that we went to the beach.

questions.def: "Enough" follows the adjective it modifies.
questions.question: He is not ___ to drive a car.

questions.def: "Such" is used before "a + adjective + noun".
questions.question: I had ___ a good time that I forgot my problems.
